title: Andy Shallal: ‘I Didn’t Have to Come Here, I Chose to Come Here’
main_content:
When we interviewed Iraqi-American Andy Shallal at his Washington, D.C. restaurant, we did more laughing than talking.

Shallal, 61, was born in Iraq. In 1966, his father, a diplomat, was assigned to the United States. Two years later, when Saddam Hussein seized power in Iraq, Shallal’s father was out of political favor.

The family could no longer return to their homeland.

Shallal attended Catholic University in Washington, D.C. and medical school at Howard University.

His passions – food, friends, and expression – led him to open his restaurant called Busboys and Poets, in 2005. There, customers can eat, read, watch performances, and express their political views freely.

Shallal expresses himself artistically in many ways.

questions.question: Why couldn’t Shallal and his family return to Iraq?
options: His father lost his diplomatic position due to a political shift.
They were not allowed to enter the country due to travel restrictions.
They feared for their safety after Saddam Hussein came to power.
Shallal's mother was not a citizen.
questions.answer: His father lost his diplomatic position due to a political shift.

questions.question: When did Shallal open his restaurant?
What can customers do at Busboys and Poets?
options: Participate in daily live cooking contests.
Eat, read, watch performances, and express political views.
questions.answer: Eat, read, watch performances, and express political views.
